stem: In Valmiki's Ramayana, when Ravana courts the captive Sita in the Ashoka grove, what does she place between herself and him before answering?
options: a small lit lamp of clay
a fold of her own sari
a single blade of grass
the jewel from her hair
why: Sita puts a blade of grass between herself and Ravana and speaks through it, refusing even to address him directly; the jewel from her hair she later gives to Hanuman as a token for Rama. Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda.

es.stem: En el Ramayana de Valmiki, cuando Ravana corteja a Sita, su cautiva, en el bosque de Ashoka, ¿qué pone ella entre los dos antes de responderle?
options: una pequeña lámpara de barro
un pliegue de su propio sari
una sola brizna de hierba
la joya de su cabello
es.why: Sita pone una brizna de hierba entre ella y Ravana y le habla a través de ella, negándose incluso a dirigirse a él directamente; la joya de su cabello se la da después a Hanuman como señal para Rama. Ramayana de Valmiki, Sundara Kanda.

stem: In the Mahabharata's tale of Nala and Damayanti, four gods take Nala's form at her svayamvara (bride's choice). How does Damayanti tell the real Nala apart?
options: only he bears the marks of a mortal body
only he answers when she calls his name
only he wears the ring she sent to him
a swan lands right at his feet to show her
why: At her prayer the gods show their signs: they do not sweat or blink, cast no shadow, their garlands stay fresh and their feet do not touch the ground. Nala alone has a shadow, sweat, dust and a fading garland. Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana.

es.stem: En el relato de Nala y Damayanti del Mahabharata, cuatro dioses toman la forma de Nala en su svayamvara (elección de esposo). ¿Cómo distingue Damayanti al verdadero Nala?
options: solo él tiene las señales de un cuerpo mortal
solo él responde cuando ella dice su nombre
solo él lleva el anillo que ella le envió
un cisne se posa a sus pies para mostrárselo
es.why: Ante su ruego, los dioses muestran sus señales: no sudan ni parpadean, no dan sombra, sus guirnaldas siguen frescas y sus pies no tocan el suelo. Solo Nala tiene sombra, sudor, polvo y una guirnalda que se marchita. Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Nalopakhyana.

stem: According to the Periya Puranam, who feeds the child Sambandar milk from a golden cup beside the temple tank at Sirkazhi?
options: the sage Agastya, first teacher of Tamil
the poet-saint Karaikkal Ammaiyar
the saint Appar, his elder companion
the Goddess Parvati, Shiva's consort
why: While his father bathes, the crying child is fed by the Goddess, Shiva's consort, with milk of divine wisdom; when his father asks who fed him, the boy sings his first hymn. Periya Puranam, life of Tirujnana Sambandar.
source: Sekkizhar, Periya Puranam (Tirujnana Sambandar Nayanar Puranam)

es.stem: Según el Periya Puranam, ¿quién le da al niño Sambandar leche en una copa de oro junto al estanque del templo de Sirkazhi?
options: el sabio Agastya, primer maestro del tamil
la poeta santa Karaikkal Ammaiyar
el santo Appar, su compañero mayor
la diosa Parvati, consorte de Shiva
es.why: Mientras su padre se baña, la diosa, consorte de Shiva, alimenta al niño que llora con leche de sabiduría divina; cuando su padre pregunta quién le dio de comer, el niño canta su primer himno. Periya Puranam, vida de Tirujnana Sambandar.

stem: In the Varkari tradition of Maharashtra, why does Vitthal at Pandharpur stand on a brick?
options: Jnaneshwar laid it as the shrine's very first stone
Pundalik gave it to him while tending his parents
Namdev set it there so the god would never leave
Janabai offered it as a seat while grinding grain
why: God comes to Pundalik, who is caring for his parents; Pundalik gives him a brick, tossing it out, to stand on until he is done, and Vitthal waits there still, hands on hips. Varkari tradition of Pandharpur.
source: Varkari tradition; Pandurang Mahatmya and the abhangas of the Varkari saints

es.stem: En la tradición varkari de Maharashtra, ¿por qué Vitthal, en Pandharpur, está de pie sobre un ladrillo?
options: Jnaneshwar lo puso como primera piedra del templo
Pundalik se lo lanzó mientras atendía a sus padres
Namdev lo colocó para que el dios nunca se fuera
Janabai se lo ofreció de asiento mientras molía grano
es.why: Dios llega a ver a Pundalik, que está cuidando a sus padres; Pundalik le lanza un ladrillo para que espere de pie hasta que termine, y Vitthal sigue allí esperando, con las manos en la cintura. Tradición varkari de Pandharpur.

stem: In the Bhagavata Purana, why does King Bali still grant the dwarf Vamana three steps of land after his teacher Shukra warns that the boy is Vishnu?
options: he hopes to win Vishnu's help against Indra
he fears a curse from the young brahmin boy
he will not take back a promise once given
he doubts his teacher's word about the boy
why: Bali answers Shukra that, as Prahlada's grandson, he will not break his word: the earth can bear any weight except a liar. He pours the water and gives the gift. Bhagavata Purana 8.20.

es.stem: En el Bhagavata Purana, ¿por qué el rey Bali le concede al enano Vamana tres pasos de tierra aun después de que su maestro Shukra le advierte que el niño es Vishnu?
options: espera ganar la ayuda de Vishnu contra Indra
teme una maldición del joven brahmán
no retira una promesa una vez dada
duda de lo que su maestro dice del niño
es.why: Bali le responde a Shukra que, como nieto de Prahlada, no romperá su palabra: la tierra puede soportar cualquier peso menos el de un mentiroso. Vierte el agua y entrega el don. Bhagavata Purana 8.20.

stem: Shankara's Advaita Vedanta explains bondage with a rope mistaken for a snake. At dusk a traveler takes a tree stump for a man and is afraid. On Shankara's reasoning, what makes the 'man' go away?
options: the man walking off down the road by himself
a torch held up to drive the man off the road
the stump accepted as a real form of the man
the stump seen clearly as the stump it is
why: For Advaita, an error is removed only by knowledge of what was there all along: once the rope (or stump) is seen, the snake (or man) is not chased away but found never to have been there. Shankara, Brahma Sutra Bhashya, preface; Gaudapada, Mandukya Karika 2.17-18.
source: Shankara, Brahma Sutra Bhashya (Adhyasa Bhashya); Gaudapada, Mandukya Karika 2.17-18

es.stem: El Advaita Vedanta de Shankara explica la atadura con una cuerda que se confunde con una serpiente. Al anochecer, un viajero confunde un tocón con un hombre y siente miedo. Según el razonamiento de Shankara, ¿qué hace que el 'hombre' desaparezca?
options: que el hombre se vaya solo por el camino
una antorcha alzada para echarlo del camino
aceptar el tocón como forma real del hombre
ver con claridad que el tocón es un tocón
es.why: Para el Advaita, un error solo se quita conociendo lo que siempre estuvo ahí: cuando se ve la cuerda (o el tocón), la serpiente (o el hombre) no se ahuyenta, sino que se descubre que nunca estuvo. Shankara, Brahma Sutra Bhashya, prefacio; Gaudapada, Mandukya Karika 2.17-18.

stem: In the Mahabharata's story of Savitri, how does Savitri win back her husband Satyavan's life from Yama, the god of death?
why: Savitri follows Yama as he carries Satyavan's life away and speaks of friendship, dharma and the good; pleased, Yama grants boons, anything but Satyavan's life. She at last asks for sons of her own by Satyavan (or, in the final boon, for his life itself), and Yama releases him. Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Pativrata-mahatmya Parva.
source: Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Pativrata-mahatmya Parva (Savitri Upakhyana)

rubric.point: Says she follows Yama when he takes Satyavan and keeps speaking with him (about dharma, friendship or the good), which pleases him. Saying only that she 'begged' or 'cried' counts as partly.

Says Yama grants her boons and that a boon is what gives Satyavan back: either her request for sons of her own by Satyavan, which can't be kept without him, or a final request for his life once Yama tells her to choose. Either telling counts.
Names earlier boons, such as sight and kingdom for her father-in-law or sons for her own father (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En la historia de Savitri del Mahabharata, ¿cómo recupera Savitri la vida de su esposo Satyavan de manos de Yama, el dios de la muerte?
es.why: Savitri sigue a Yama mientras se lleva la vida de Satyavan y le habla de la amistad, del dharma y de los buenos; complacido, Yama le concede dones, cualquier cosa menos la vida de Satyavan. Al final ella pide hijos propios con Satyavan (o, en el último don, su vida misma), y Yama lo libera. Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Pativrata-mahatmya Parva.

stem: In the Bhagavata Purana, Kunti prays to Krishna before he leaves for Dwaraka. What unusual gift does she ask for, and why?
why: Kunti asks that troubles come to her again and again, because in trouble she always saw Krishna, and seeing him ends the round of births; she adds that wealth, birth, learning and beauty can make people too proud to call on God. Bhagavata Purana 1.8.25-26.

rubric.point: Says she asks for troubles, hardship or calamities to come again and again. Asking for 'protection' or 'peace' does not count.
Says why: in her troubles she saw or remembered Krishna, and seeing him frees one from rebirth or keeps her close to God. Only 'to grow stronger' counts as partly.
Mentions that wealth, high birth, learning or beauty can make a person too proud to turn to God, or names the dangers he saved the Pandavas from (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el Bhagavata Purana, Kunti le reza a Krishna antes de que él parta hacia Dwaraka. ¿Qué don poco común le pide, y por qué?
es.why: Kunti pide que las desgracias le lleguen una y otra vez, porque en las desgracias siempre vio a Krishna, y verlo pone fin al ciclo de los nacimientos; añade que la riqueza, el linaje, el saber y la belleza pueden volver a alguien demasiado orgulloso para acudir a Dios. Bhagavata Purana 1.8.25-26.
